question.prompt: Solve \(\{x+y=3,\ y+z=5,\ x+z=4\}\). (Give the values of \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\), in this order, separated by commas.)

solutions.explanation: Adding the three equations gives \(2(x+y+z)=12\), so \(x+y+z=6\). Subtracting each equation in turn gives \(z=6-3=3\), \(x=6-5=1\), and \(y=6-4=2\).
solutions.title: Add all three equations

solutions.explanation:
Expressing both \(y\) and \(z\) in terms of \(x\) reduces the remaining equation to one unknown. From \(x+y=3\) and \(x+z=4\), we have \(y=3-x\) and \(z=4-x\). Substituting into \(y+z=5\) gives
\[
(3-x)+(4-x)=5,
\]
so \(7-2x=5\) and \(x=1\). Then \(y=3-1=2\) and \(z=4-1=3\). The requested values are \(1,2,3\).
